case.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
case.note: 2,877 customers have a phone number. 56 have verified consent. The audience code counts must be the second.

trace.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
trace.answer:
I proposed the campaign, but only to 56 customers, not to everyone who gave us a phone number. Nothing has been sent, and a person has to approve it first.

Of 2,958 customers with a phone number, only 56 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. Our messaging policy allows marketing texts only to those customers. Customers who just gave us a number when ordering don't qualify [messaging: Who may receive marketing texts].

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend, through Sunday Oct 25. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out"

The 10% is under the 15% cap, and the message has an expiry date, "one per customer" and the restaurant name [messaging: Offers in messages] [messaging: Required wording]. The system's checks on the discount, the wording and the audience all passed. The text also has to go out between 9am and 8pm local time [messaging: Quiet hours].

case.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I can't set up that text. Two of our messaging rules rule it out.

Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message [messaging: Offers in messages]. A 25% discount is also over the 20% limit that applies without the owner's approval [messaging: Offers in messages].

I could propose a different campaign instead. It would offer up to 20% off other items, expire within 7 days, and be limited to one use per customer. It would go only to customers who ordered in the last 90 days and have a phone number, and who haven't unsubscribed. Each person could get at most two marketing texts a month [messaging: Who may receive texts]. It would be sent between 8am and 9pm Mountain time [messaging: Quiet hours]. Tell me which items and how you define "regulars," and I'll size the audience and draft the message.

case.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.

trace.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
trace.answer:
I haven't comped anything. I proposed a notification to the owner, and it is pending until a person approves it.

A $60 comp is over the $25 a manager can comp on one ticket. Anything above that needs the owner, who can be reached by text during service [house: Comps]. A cold dish is a food-quality complaint, which is a valid reason for a comp [house: Comps]. The proposal asks the owner to approve a $60 comp for table 12.

The data doesn't record table numbers, so I couldn't match this to a specific order. I found two in-store orders from the evening of Oct 23 in that range. Order 101117 has $59.62 in gross sales and a $65.73 total. Order 101099 has $50.54 in gross sales and a $64.94 total. Neither is confirmed as table 12, so the proposal has no order attached. Please confirm the order before the comp is applied.

Comps should also stay under 1% of the week's gross sales. If a week goes over, the owner reviews every comp from that week [house: Comps].
